title: Five Principles for Small UX Teams
intro: A decision template for small teams: move fast without guessing.

topics.title: Five Principles for Small UX Teams

learn.title: Five principles
learn.text:
**1. Short-term** — design for the next 6–8 months and today's technology
**2. Clear writing over minimalism** — when in doubt, be explicit
**3. Just in time** — information at the point of need
**4. Best practice** — don't reinvent problems that are already solved
**5. Behaviour over opinion** — what users do, not what they say

try.q: How far ahead should a small team design?
try.explain: Realistic users and tech stack, not a hypothetical future at scale.

learn.title: Documentation and patterns
learn.text:
Collaborate early and often with other UXers so decisions are shared and documented — **optimising for 6–8 months in the future**, when a different designer picks it up. (Only applies if there's more than one UXer.)

**Do:** look for a handful of successful examples of a similar pattern before designing one.
**Don't:** design for hypothetical future behaviour, especially based on a single example.

try.q: Before inventing a pattern, what should you look for?
options: A handful of successful examples of it
A design system component that already exists

learn.title: Writing and research
learn.text:
“Use as few words as possible — but add the words that make it explicit.” Minimalism is not the goal; clarity is.

And prefer **usability tests and analytics over preference surveys** when time is short: base new designs on how generative research predicts behaviour will change, not on hypotheticals.

test.explain: Though most of it applies more widely.

test.q: What does “clear writing over minimalism” mean?
options: Add the words that make it explicit
Write longer help text for each field
test.explain: As few words as possible, but no fewer.

options: A different designer will pick it up
Design systems are usually revised twice a year

test.q: What is the risk of designing for hypothetical future behaviour?
options: It's often based on a single example
It usually conflicts with the design system
test.explain: Use generative research to predict realistic change instead.
Guidelines, and most apply beyond startups.
